# Knowledge interview

## Overview
The AI never invents business rules (ADR 0009). It asks the person who knows, writes it down, and the expert only **talks and validates**. Exceptions are where unwritten knowledge hides, so the interview spends most of its time there.

## When to use
- A requirement needs a rule that is not in `aidlc/knowledge/` (instead of guessing).
- Draft `BR-NNN` from reverse engineering wait for confirmation.
- The person says "only Maria knows how month-end closing works".

## Process
1. Agree on the topic and the expert. Keep the session short (20–30 minutes); say so.
2. Read what exists: `aidlc/knowledge/glossary.md`, rules and procedures on the topic, draft rules that `governs` the same paths.
3. Interview one question at a time (protocol `questions`):
   - the normal case, in their words;
   - **exceptions**: "when does this not apply?", "who can override it?", "what happens at exactly the limit?";
   - examples with real-looking values (they become tests in Construction);
   - where it is written today, if anywhere (it goes into `evidence`).
4. Write each rule as `aidlc/knowledge/rules/BR-NNN-<slug>.md` (procedures in `knowledge/procedures/PR-NNN-…`) from `ra-aidlc stage template memory-item`: `owner` = the expert, `evidence` (the interview and any written source), `review_by` (a date, usually 6–12 months), Given/When/Then examples. Status `draft` until the expert reads it back; `accepted` with `approved_by` only after their yes. Terms become glossary rows.
5. For a draft rule from code that the expert says is wrong: mark it `rejected` and tell the person the code may have a bug.
6. If two sources disagree, set `disputed` and ask both owners; never pick a side silently.
7. Add INDEX lines and run `ra-aidlc gate` (`frontmatter` checks owners on accepted rules).

## Common rationalizations
| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I can infer the rule from the code." | The code shows behaviour; only the owner knows if it is the rule or a bug. |
| "The expert is busy, I'll fill the gaps." | Then the gap stays a question, tagged `[assumption]`, not a rule. |

## Red flags
- An accepted rule without an `owner`.
- Recording who knows what beyond name and role, or evaluating people. The goal is to spread knowledge, not to rate anyone. `experts.md` stays off unless the team decided otherwise.

## Verification
- `ra-aidlc gate` passes `frontmatter`; requirements citing the rule no longer warn about a draft rule.
